assessment_basis: Substantive reading of cached official USENIX program abstracts; no fresh source fetch or full-paper review claimed.

records.review_reason: Surveys how social expectations and emotions shape engagement with protective practices. Supports designing usable prevention guidance and understanding why advice is not adopted.
records.limitation: Self-reported associations in 496 U.S. respondents do not establish reduced cybercrime victimisation.

records.review_reason: Audits authentication policies at 135 universities, identifying outdated practices and uneven multi-factor deployment. Supports assessing organisational account-security weaknesses and diffusion of protective guidance.
records.limitation: Policy compliance does not measure compromise rates; standards discussed reflect the study period.

records.review_reason: Examines culturally situated household privacy negotiations, including camera use and family power. Potential context for technology-enabled surveillance, but the abstract does not investigate abuse or crime.
records.limitation: Qualitative household practices must not be generalised into prevalence or claims of unlawful surveillance.

records.review_reason: Identifies confusing terminology in app privacy labels through qualitative and quantitative studies. General disclosure-comprehension research with no concrete cybercrime or investigative contribution.
records.limitation: The studies evaluate interpretation, not label accuracy, malicious apps or resulting harms.

records.review_reason: Studies forced reciprocity in messaging, social profiles and smart-home visibility. Potential relevance to interpersonal privacy pressure, but abuse and investigation are not evaluated.
records.limitation: Survey responses from 802 U.S. participants do not establish how coercive relationships use these settings.

records.review_reason: Tracks novice password-manager use over three months and finds ignored credential-audit flags and persistent adoption friction. Supports practical credential-protection education.
records.limitation: Thirty-seven participants and a single commercial product; outcomes are usability and reported behaviour, not prevented account takeover.

records.review_reason: Observes actual Android permission states and revocations alongside users' explanations. Supports understanding controls and awareness gaps relevant to mobile privacy protection.
records.limitation: A 132-person field study; permission changes are not direct evidence of malware, compromise or successful mitigation.

records.review_reason: Evaluates a redesigned mobile-app privacy label for comprehension and task speed. The abstract addresses general interface design rather than cybercrime, abuse or investigation.
records.limitation: A controlled study with 200 participants does not establish field adoption or protection against harmful apps.

records.review_reason: Compares code-writing, reading and fixing tasks as methods for studying secure development. Supports critical appraisal of evidence about developer behaviour and security APIs.
records.limitation: Preliminary findings from encryption tasks may not generalise across languages or development contexts.

records.review_reason: Documents credential-sharing strategies and security concessions, including reuse between personal and shared accounts. Relevant to interpreting account access and designing account-protection interventions.
records.limitation: Self-reported sharing does not identify malicious access or establish that a particular account has one operator.

records.review_reason: Examines emotional influences on employees' cybersecurity decisions and proposes a framework for protective behaviour. Supports human-centred security training and operational support.
records.limitation: Qualitative and survey findings do not validate the effectiveness of the proposed recommendations.

records.review_reason: Develops ways for domestic robots to communicate sensor and connectivity states. The abstract focuses on general privacy signalling without a concrete abuse or investigative problem.
records.limitation: Trust, preferences and comprehensibility ratings do not establish privacy protection in deployment.

records.review_reason: Co-designs ways to inform bystanders about live streaming and unintentional capture. Supports prevention of unwanted disclosure and analysis of consent in public recording.
records.limitation: Twenty-one participants and design ideation; no deployed intervention or abuse reduction was assessed.

records.review_reason: Evaluates usability of four differential-privacy libraries for data practitioners. Useful privacy engineering research, but no specific cybercrime or investigative application is established.
records.limitation: Twenty-four practitioners; library usability should not be confused with correctness of privacy guarantees.

records.review_reason: Surveys human-centred cybersecurity researchers about barriers to engaging practitioners. Supports judging whether research can be translated into usable operational guidance.
records.limitation: Researcher reports do not substitute for practitioner evaluation or evidence of improved security outcomes.

records.review_reason: Assesses privacy claims in digital public goods and examines three implementations for actual threats. Supports scrutiny of assurances around identity and public-service data.
records.limitation: The selected case studies and standard review are not a complete audit of all digital public goods.

records.review_reason: Surveys development teams' privacy concepts, knowledge and regulatory concerns. The abstract offers general privacy-development guidance without a concrete cybercrime or investigative link.
records.limitation: Self-reported knowledge and practices from 362 respondents do not establish product security or legal compliance.

records.review_reason: Examines shadow IT and employees' risk attitudes in one organisation. Supports understanding divergence between sanctioned systems and actual practices during organisational investigations.
records.limitation: A single-company case study; unsanctioned use is not itself proof of malicious intent or an incident.

records.review_reason: Tests stereotype-related attitudes and self-assessed knowledge in security and privacy. Its workforce-diversity contribution is not directly tied to cybercrime or investigative practice.
records.limitation: The study reports little overall stereotype-threat evidence; subgroup differences do not establish protective outcomes.

records.review_reason: Tests how app-label attributes influence perceived risk and willingness to install apps. General privacy-choice research without a concrete investigative or abuse-prevention evaluation.
records.limitation: Large self-reported odds shifts are not equivalent to actual installation behaviour or reduced harm.

records.review_reason: Interviews OT security professionals about governance, communication and expertise barriers. Supports understanding organisational constraints in critical-infrastructure security and incident preparedness.
records.limitation: Thirty-three UK interviews; consultancy recommendations were not evaluated as interventions.

records.review_reason: Investigates why experienced security managers cannot resolve friction between controls and daily work. Supports interpreting policy workarounds and designing workable protective procedures.
records.limitation: Fourteen interviews and proposed remedies do not establish causation or reduced incident rates.

records.review_reason: Surveys prospective digital-euro users about features, security and privacy preferences. The abstract concerns payment-system design without a concrete fraud, cybercrime or investigative contribution.
records.limitation: Preferences in an Austrian survey should not be treated as observed adoption or measured financial crime risks.

records.review_reason: Examines password-manager setup strategies, distrust and incomplete credential migration. Supports practical account-protection guidance and identifying limits of nominal tool adoption.
records.limitation: Product reviews and 279 survey respondents do not establish security effectiveness after deployment.

records.review_reason: Tracks companies' continued use of password expiry after guidance changed. Supports evaluation of how organisations adopt or resist evidence-based authentication advice.
records.limitation: Different survey samples and self-reported policy use do not establish causal effects on compromise.

records.review_reason: Separates interface and demographic explanations for adoption of generated passwords. Supports designing and evaluating credential-protection interventions.
records.limitation: A study of 853 participants measures password choice, not prevented attacks or long-term adherence.

records.review_reason: Designs personalised physical objects for second-factor authentication and studies daily use. Potential support for account security, but the investigation focuses on product usability rather than abuse or response.
records.limitation: A one-week field trial with fifteen users does not establish resistance to attack or broad adoption.

records.review_reason: Tests risk-framing interventions that encourage stronger user-selected passwords. Supports empirical assessment of account-protection education and choice design.
records.limitation: Observed strength changes do not establish reduced account takeover or durable behaviour change.

records.review_reason: Evaluates users' ability to identify and correct unsafe smart-home automation rules. Relevant to understanding unintended access and whether analysis tools communicate security issues effectively.
records.limitation: Survey tasks with 447 participants are not an audit of deployed homes or malicious automation.

records.review_reason: Investigates recruitment barriers for studies involving professional developers. Supports evaluating sample selection and the practical credibility of secure-development research.
records.limitation: Thirty interviews concern participation incentives and constraints, not tested software security outcomes.

records.review_reason: Systematises power-analysis information and identifies underpowered developer-security studies. Supports judging evidentiary strength and planning reliable human-centred security research.
records.limitation: Meta-analysis concerns the selected literature; individual studies require assessment rather than blanket dismissal.

records.review_reason: Identifies accessibility and security barriers in a cryptocurrency wallet and iteratively evaluates a redesign. Supports inclusive financial-asset protection and understanding wallet-user difficulties.
records.limitation: Forty-four participants; usability gains do not establish resistance to theft, phishing or malicious transactions.

records.review_reason: Interviews youth and parents about online security knowledge and learning practices. Supports designing age-appropriate prevention guidance and understanding limits of monitoring-based education.
records.limitation: Forty dyads and qualitative associations do not establish which parenting approach prevents victimisation.

records.review_reason: Prototypes assistance for blind users to detect and redact private image content. Supports reducing unintended disclosure and evaluating accessibility needs in protective tools.
records.limitation: An exploratory design-probe study; privacy detection accuracy and field effectiveness require further evidence.

records.review_reason: Studies community oversight of apps and permissions over four weeks. Supports collaborative prevention and understanding trust and expertise constraints in shared security assistance.
records.limitation: Reported awareness and participation do not establish fewer malicious apps or compromised devices.

records.review_reason: Examines social expectations influencing willingness to use technologies that make sensitive inferences. Potential context for privacy-risk persuasion, but no specific cybercrime or abuse scenario is investigated.
records.limitation: Vignette choices and social-norm effects do not establish real-world adoption or harm.

records.review_reason: Interviews voluntary secure-email adopters and finds limited actual encrypted exchange despite privacy motivation. Supports evaluating communication-protection adoption and its practical limits.
records.limitation: Participant perceptions and use reports do not independently verify service security or confidentiality.

records.review_reason: Develops a behavioural scale covering technical and social smartphone protection practices. Supports critical measurement of prevention behaviour in research and education.
records.limitation: Psychometric reliability does not prove that scale scores predict compromise or actual defensive effectiveness.

records.review_reason: Examines mental models of electronic health records in Germany. The abstract addresses general patient privacy expectations rather than cybercrime, abuse investigation or incident response.
records.limitation: Misconceptions about access and data exchange are not evidence that records were unlawfully accessed.

records.review_reason: Collects privacy-conscious smart-home users' experiences of transparency and control. Potential context for household surveillance safeguards, but no concrete abuse or investigative problem is evaluated.
records.limitation: Thirty-two power users are not representative of ordinary households; design ideas remain unevaluated.

records.review_reason: Interviews smart-lock users about concerns, mitigations and indifference to access risks. Supports interpreting how household access controls are understood and used.
records.limitation: Twenty-nine interviews do not independently test lock exploitability or demonstrate that perceived mitigations prevent intrusion.

records.review_reason: Surveys expected privacy effects of AI across ten countries. The contribution is broad public attitudes and priorities rather than a concrete cybercrime or investigative method.
records.limitation: Expectations, even when well reasoned, do not measure actual AI abuse or resulting harms.

records.review_reason: Evaluates indicators intended to distinguish secure virtual-reality transitions. Supports research on trustworthy interface cues and reducing confusion around virtual destinations.
records.limitation: The small user study measures interpretation and task performance, not resistance to actual impersonation campaigns.

records.review_reason: Integrates online-safety microlearning into verification tasks and evaluates learning over fifteen days. Supports assessment of accessible prevention education in routine online interactions.
records.limitation: Learning and perceived-usability findings do not establish bot resistance, lasting behaviour change or reduced victimisation.

records.review_reason: Studies how knowledgeable peers provide security advice and develops ways to support their informal assistance. Relevant to community prevention and practical guidance networks.
records.limitation: Thirteen interviews and co-design sessions do not evaluate the security outcomes of the proposed support.

records.review_reason: Examines practitioners' mental models of machine-learning attacks and workflow vulnerabilities. Supports threat communication and understanding blind spots in AI-system security analysis.
records.limitation: Qualitative perspectives are not an adversarial robustness test or a measured reduction in exploitable vulnerabilities.

records.review_reason: Replicates differential-privacy explanations with German participants and compares data-sharing attitudes. The abstract concerns general privacy communication without a concrete investigative or abuse problem.
records.limitation: Cross-sample willingness differences do not establish cultural causes or actual data-sharing behaviour.

records.review_reason: Develops metaphors for differential privacy and evaluates comprehension. General explanation-design research, without a specific cybercrime or investigative contribution.
records.limitation: Thirty interviews reveal comprehension limits; the metaphors do not establish correctness of a deployed privacy mechanism.

records.review_reason: Tests an identity-wallet prototype and uncovers misunderstandings about identifiers, QR journeys and control of disclosures. Supports assessment of identity-system usability and misplaced confidence.
records.limitation: Thirty participants and a prototype; it does not demonstrate identity fraud prevention or validate wallet security.

records.review_reason: Investigates security and usability problems in TPM library APIs. Supports understanding how implementation choices can weaken hardware-backed security and integrity mechanisms.
records.limitation: Nine participants and one principal API; claims about other libraries need separate verification.

records.review_reason: Evaluates a verifiable voting design and users' ability to detect manipulation. Directly relevant to human verification of election-integrity evidence.
records.limitation: The user study does not independently establish end-to-end cryptographic correctness or field election security.

records.review_reason: Synthesises usability methods for privacy-choice interfaces and proposes an evaluation framework. General privacy-management methodology without a concrete cybercrime or investigative application.
records.limitation: The framework is not itself evidence that a particular choice mechanism is protective or lawful.

records.review_reason: Develops and evaluates a remote study environment for security information workers. Supports conducting and critically assessing research with practitioners who are hard to recruit in person.
records.limitation: Prototype evaluations and positive feedback do not establish equivalence to every laboratory or operational setting.

records.review_reason: Finds misalignment between intended privacy constructs and how survey participants interpret scale statements. Supports careful interpretation of research evidence used in prevention and victim-support work.
records.limitation: Results caution against overinterpreting scales; they do not invalidate every use or provide a universally validated replacement.

records.review_reason: Uses three measurement-panel case studies to examine recruitment, retention and intrusive data collection. Supports evaluating bias and evidence quality in longitudinal security-behaviour research.
records.limitation: Practical experience in selected panels may not generalise to different populations or monitoring designs.

records.review_reason: Replicates survey-generalizability research and compares crowdsourcing samples with probabilistic data. Supports assessing bot contamination, sample bias and credibility of online security studies.
records.limitation: Findings are specific to sampled platforms, settings and question types; no platform guarantees representative evidence.

records.review_reason: Investigates misinformation encountered and managed in private WhatsApp groups. Directly supports understanding harmful-content propagation, family pressures and moderation constraints in encrypted communications.
records.limitation: Sixteen U.S. student interviews during COVID-19 do not estimate global misinformation prevalence or validate proposed interventions.

records.review_reason: Studies adoption and misconceptions about digital COVID certificates in Germany. The abstract addresses general privacy attitudes and convenience rather than certificate fraud or an investigative method.
records.limitation: Results from the 2021 survey context are not current legal guidance or evidence of credential integrity.

records.review_reason: Observes administrators configuring risk-based authentication against malicious login attempts. Directly relevant to the practical reliability of account-protection controls and their defaults.
records.limitation: Twenty-eight administrators used a mock-up; configurations were not tested against production attacks.

records.review_reason: Evaluates programming aids for secure password authentication with freelance developers. Supports judging how documentation and code resources affect protective implementations.
records.limitation: The study's relative secure-code gains concern specific tasks and controls, not guaranteed application security.

records.review_reason: Designs a password-policy description language to help generators produce acceptable credentials and evaluates feasibility. Supports reducing friction that undermines credential protection.
records.limitation: Prototype feasibility and a 25-person developer study do not establish broad website adoption or reduced compromise.

records.review_reason: Audits popular websites for weak-password acceptance and other policy choices. Supports identifying gaps between authentication guidance and deployed account protections.
records.limitation: The 120-site sample is not a census, and policy observations alone do not establish compromise rates.

records.review_reason: Compares browser prompts encouraging generated passwords and examines reasons for adoption. Supports evaluating interventions against password reuse and weak credentials.
records.limitation: Results from 558 participants do not show long-term adherence or prevented account takeover.

records.review_reason: Proposes hardware-backed personhood attestation as an alternative to CAPTCHAs and evaluates a public demonstration. Directly relevant to bot-abuse controls and accessibility trade-offs.
records.limitation: User preference and demo performance do not establish universal personhood, resistance to organised abuse or suitability for users without hardware.

records.review_reason: Studies permission prompts for continuously listening proactive assistants. Its contribution concerns general privacy-control preferences without a concrete abuse or investigative evaluation.
records.limitation: Wizard-of-Oz sessions with 23 pairs do not evaluate a deployed assistant's security or actual data handling.

records.review_reason: Examines social norms and sensitive inferences from wearable and smart-home sensor data. Broad collective-privacy research without a specific cybercrime or investigative contribution.
records.limitation: Qualitative reactions to plausible inferences do not establish that those inferences were made or misused.

records.review_reason: Prototypes automatic detection of phone handovers to protect data during temporary sharing. Relevant to preventing unauthorised access and understanding interpersonal device-sharing risks.
records.limitation: Small gesture and session evaluations do not establish robustness against deliberate adversaries or all sharing contexts.

records.review_reason: Finds that users designate locations accessible to unwanted adversaries as trusted phone-unlock areas. Directly relevant to unauthorised physical access and weak real-world authentication boundaries.
records.limitation: Field observations classify potential access risk; they do not show that actual intrusions occurred.

records.review_reason: Audits employee-facing password policies in German companies against guidance. Supports examining organisational authentication practices and why weak or burdensome controls persist.
records.limitation: Self-reported policies from 83 companies do not establish their complete implementation or security outcomes.

records.review_reason: Tests pattern blocklists against simulated guessing attacks while evaluating usability. Directly relevant to mitigating unauthorised smartphone access.
records.limitation: Simulated attacker success and short-term recall do not establish resistance to every attack or long-term behaviour.

records.review_reason: Studies prospective adoption and misconceptions about a COVID exposure-notification app. The abstract addresses public communication and privacy expectations, not a concrete cybercrime or investigative issue.
records.limitation: Intentions before release do not establish actual use, epidemiological effectiveness or present app behaviour.

records.review_reason: Examines users' understanding of browser-extension privileges and associated data-access threats. Directly relevant to abuse of trusted extensions and practical warning design.
records.limitation: Survey reports from 353 participants do not independently audit extensions or establish actual malicious access.

records.review_reason: Replicates research on how media shapes technical users' understanding of hacking. Supports interpreting misconceptions that may influence practitioners and the advice they give others.
records.limitation: Twenty-three qualitative participants; recognition of fictional inaccuracies is not an operational skill assessment.

records.review_reason: Compares smartphone-platform users' knowledge and attitudes to assess generalizability of security studies. Supports critical evaluation of sample selection and platform-specific claims.
records.limitation: A U.S. survey and Prolific comparison do not establish that platform choice causes knowledge differences.

records.review_reason: Explores understanding of rights and explanations for solely automated decisions. General governance and interface research without a concrete cybercrime or investigative application.
records.limitation: Survey views and historical regulatory interpretation are not current legal advice or evidence of discriminatory outcomes.

records.review_reason: Examines Android tracking and whether apps and libraries obtain consent. Directly relevant to investigating undisclosed data collection and evaluating technical responsibility across the ecosystem.
records.limitation: Potential legal violations are the authors' analysis in the study context; current legal status and individual cases require separate assessment.

records.review_reason: Examines Canadians' responses to privacy-violation scenarios and difficulties exercising rights. Potential context for reporting and remedy after data misuse, but no concrete investigation is evaluated.
records.limitation: Hypothetical responses and moral judgments do not establish actual legal violations or effective remedies.

records.review_reason: Co-designs improvements to data-access downloads so people can locate and interpret information held about them. Supports understanding the practical utility and limitations of personal-data archives.
records.limitation: Focus groups with 42 participants do not establish evidentiary completeness or forensic integrity of provider downloads.

records.review_reason: Studies reactions to facial-recognition deployments, including bias and broad surveillance concerns. Potential context for assessing trust in investigative technology, but accuracy and investigative outcomes are not evaluated.
records.limitation: Scenario reactions from 123 participants do not measure recognition error rates or actual discriminatory deployment.

records.review_reason: Evaluates trusted assistance for blind users facing visual CAPTCHA barriers. Supports accessible anti-abuse mechanisms and understanding privacy and dependency trade-offs.
records.limitation: An exploratory role-play study with ten pairs does not establish bot resistance or the security of remote assistance in deployment.
